THE ACTUAL WORKSHEET

Exactly what you’ll print.

This is the real sheet — the same file the buttons above hand you. Title, instructions, the activity itself, and a grown-up answer line where it helps.

Download Free Worksheet ↓ Play This Activity Online ↗

The PDF is a real printable file (A4, prints fine on US Letter). The print button prints only the worksheet — never the website around it. No sign-up, nothing stored.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Blending is the act of squashing separate sounds into one word — the exact skill reading demands. The sheet shows boxes for each sound; saying each sound as its letter is written makes the blending physical.

  • Blending three sounds into a word
  • Writing the letters for each sound
  • Reading back the written word
  • Sound-by-sound patience
HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. You are the sound machine

    Paper cannot play audio — that is your job. Say the sound (a pure “sss”, not “suh” or the letter name) and let your child copy it.

  2. Say the picture words together

    Name every picture before starting. The activity is the sound, not the guessing of what the picture is.

  3. Little sounds, short sessions

    Two rows done well is a full phonics session. Stop while the ears are still fresh.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Sounds, not letter names

The letter is m, but the sound is “mmm”. Stretch the sounds you can hold (mmm, sss, fff) and keep stops snappy (t, p, k).

Play the online game afterwards

Every worksheet has a matching game at kiddo.school where the sounds are played aloud — paper first, screen second works beautifully.

Answers are at the bottom

Each phonics sheet ends with a grown-up answer line, so you can check together without guessing.

Answer guide

cat, sun, pig. If blending stalls, say the sounds for your child to squash together.

WHERE THIS FITS

The class and the game behind it.

This worksheet is the paper twin of Robot Sound Blender, a real game in the Phonics Adventures library. It belongs to Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole phonics collection lives at /worksheets/phonics/. Play the game on screen first, print the worksheet second — or the other way round; they practice the same skill in two languages.
